what: MCP server lifecycle (April 2026): the aide-memory MCP server is NOT a persistent daemon — it's a stdio child process Claude Code spawns at session start and kills at session end. "Recovery" from an outage happens automatically whenever a new Claude session starts with a healthy `.mcp.json`. The new `ingestPendingMemories()` function (added Apr 20) runs in `startServer()` right after MemoryStore creation, so any memories written to `.aide/pending-memories.jsonl` during an outage get ingested on the next good session start. Hooks remain independent of MCP (pure bash scripts), so blocking/correction detection still work even when MCP is down — the agent just falls back to writing the jsonl file per the instruction in detect-correction.sh.
why: User asked how MCP recovers after being down. Worth capturing: "MCP isn't a daemon" is non-obvious — users might look for a systemd service or background process. Recovery is automatic per-session. This ties the J validation findings + new ingest code together in one spot so future sessions understand the whole graceful-degradation story without re-deriving it.
